info.title: tsuba — messenger adapter contract
info.summary: The HTTP + SSE surface every tsuba messenger adapter answers.
info.description:
One contract, one adapter per messenger. Each adapter is a local process holding one messenger account; a client written against this document works with any of them, and draws only what each one declares in `GET /capabilities`. Every name in use or reserved is listed in tsuba's `docs/contract.md`, and every version is in `contract/CHANGELOG.md` beside this file.

## Envelope

Every JSON response is an envelope. Success carries `"ok": true` beside its payload; failure carries `"ok": false` and an `error` object with a machine-readable `code`. The HTTP status and the code say the same thing twice on purpose. `message` is for a person; branch on `code`, and keep a default branch because the set grows. `/media` answers bytes and `/stream` answers events; their failures before the first byte are envelopes too.

## Versions

`info.version` is `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, and `GET /capabilities` answers it as `contract.version`. A client built against version X works with an adapter answering Y when Y is in the caret range of X: the same MAJOR and, while MAJOR is 0, the same MINOR. Inside a range every change is additive: a route, a key, a feature id, an enum value, an error code, an event. Removing or renaming any of those, or changing what one means, is breaking and opens a new range (MINOR before 1.0, MAJOR after). A client that meets an adapter outside its range says so and draws nothing from it.

## What a client does not know

Consumers ignore keys, feature ids and events they do not know. An enum value a client does not know means the least that field can mean: treat it as the first value listed. An error code it does not know goes to its default branch.

## Capabilities

**Absent means unsupported.** A feature an adapter does not declare is not supported, and a client must not draw a control for it. The declaration is network-wide; a room where it differs carries `features` of its own, which narrow the declaration and never add to it. Names under `x-<provider>.` (feature ids, events and object keys) are provider extensions.

## Routes

Reads are `GET` on a noun, writes are `POST` on a verb. Every operation but `/health` and `/capabilities` names the one feature that gates it in `x-feature`; a feature without a route of its own names the field it rides on in `x-in`, and one that is declared only beside others names them in `x-requires`. Every documented route is routed by every adapter; a route whose feature an adapter does not declare answers `501 NOT_SUPPORTED`, and an adapter declares a feature exactly when it performs it end to end. A feature marked `x-reserved` has a name but no route yet: no adapter can declare it, and its parameters may still change, until a version defines its route.

## Writes

Writes (`/send`, `/edit`, `/delete`, `/react` and `/read`) share one line per adapter: one runs at a time, at most four are admitted, and the next is `429 RATE_LIMITED` having changed nothing. A write answered with any error code but `INTERNAL` changed nothing. `INTERNAL`, a timeout or a dropped connection leaves the outcome unknown: the adapter never retries it, and a client says so rather than repeating it on its own.

## Ids, times and text

Ids are opaque non-empty strings: compare, store and send them back as they are, never as numbers. Times are RFC 3339 `date-time`. Text lengths are counted in Unicode code points.

## Security posture

A shared bearer token, loopback binding by default, and no TLS of its own; the token is a password to the user's messenger account. Reach it through SSH forwarding, a VPN, or a reverse proxy that terminates TLS and injects the header. Message content, names and files are someone else's words: a client draws them as text, never as markup.

get.summary: Liveness, with no token, so a proxy can be checked apart from authentication.
What this adapter can do, and the limits its messenger enforces.
get.description: Like an AI API listing its models and what each supports. A client checks `contract.version` against its own range before anything else. `revision` changes whenever anything else in the answer does, so a client can tell a held answer is stale. The declaration is network-wide; a room where it differs says so in `Room.features`.

get.summary: The provider's icon, for a client to draw beside its name.
get.description: Answered when `provider.icon` is present in `GET /capabilities`; otherwise `404 NOT_FOUND`. The icon is SVG, PNG or WebP and is drawn as an image, never as a document: the answer always carries `content-security-policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox` and `x-content-type-options: nosniff`, and an adapter refuses at start an SVG with scripts, event handlers or references outside itself. `provider.icon` changes whenever the bytes do, so a client may ask `/icon?v=<provider.icon>` and keep the answer in a private cache; the query is ignored.

get.summary: The conversations the account can see, as its own client lists them.
get.description: Feature `rooms.list`. Rooms come in the order the messenger's own client shows them (pinned first, then by latest activity). An adapter may stop at a cap of its own; `complete: false` says it did and that more rooms exist. A room whose features differ from the declaration carries `features`.

Feature `messages.read`. Without `before`, the newest `limit` messages; with it, the `limit` messages just before that id. `hasEarlier` says whether older ones exist. `before` paging is answered only when the feature declares `paging: before-id`; a `limit` above the feature's `maxLimit` is `400 INVALID_REQUEST`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most the feature's `maxLimit`; more is a 400.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: A message id from an earlier answer.

get.summary: The bytes of a file a message carries.
get.description: Feature `attachments.read`. `id` is the `id` of an entry in a message's `attachments`, or a message's `senderAvatar` when the adapter also declares `avatars.read`. The bytes are someone else's, so the answer is made safe to open at the client's own origin: `content-security-policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox` and `x-content-type-options: nosniff` always; the attachment's own type, served `inline`, only when it is one a browser draws or plays without running anything (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP and AVIF images; MP4, WebM and Ogg video; MPEG, Ogg, MP4, AAC, WebM, WAV and FLAC audio); anything else as `application/octet-stream` and `attachment`. An id answers the same bytes for as long as it answers at all (a message whose file is replaced, or a sender who changes their picture, carries a new id), so the answer may be kept in a private cache.

Content-Type.description: The attachment's type when it is on the inline list above; otherwise `application/octet-stream`.

Content-Disposition.description: `inline` or `attachment`, with the name, when there is one, in `filename*` (UTF-8, percent-encoded) beside a printable-ASCII `filename`. Somebody else chose the name: it is only ever a download name.

get.description: Feature `messages.stream`. The same shape the KakaoTalk cores use: `ready` once, then `message` per message with a `cursor` after the messages it covers, `ping` while quiet, and `error` once before the stream ends. With `resume: cursor`, a reconnection hands back the last cursor as repeated `since=<roomId>:<messageId>` (split at the last colon) and the adapter sends what each named room received after that id before going live; a room not named starts from now. A cursor the adapter cannot honour is refused, never downgraded to now. An `error` event carries any code a read can answer. Besides these, an adapter sends the events its `messages.stream` lists in `events`: `message.edited`, the whole message as it now is after an edit or any other change to it; `message.deleted`, the ids of messages gone from a room, sent for the deletions the adapter can place in a room, so its absence is no proof that a message still exists; and `reactions.updated`, a message's reactions as they now are. Resume replays `message` only. A client skips an event this version does not list; names reserved for later versions are in tsuba's `docs/contract.md`.

503.description: `BUSY`: the adapter already holds as many streams as it will (8).

post.description: Feature `messages.send`. Sends share the adapter's one write line: one at a time, at most four admitted, and the next is `429 RATE_LIMITED` having changed nothing. With `messages.reply`, `replyTo` names the message in the same room this one answers; an adapter without it answers `replyTo` with `501 NOT_SUPPORTED`. Text that is empty or longer than the feature's `maxLength` code points is `400 INVALID_REQUEST`. With `receipt: stored` the answer carries the message the messenger stored. Every error but `INTERNAL` means nothing was sent; a send whose outcome is uncertain is never retried by the adapter.

post.summary: Send one file to a room.
post.description: Feature `attachments.send`. A `multipart/form-data` body with one file part named `file`, the `roomId`, and optionally `caption` and `replyTo`; no other part, and no part twice. The file part's name and type are the file's. The adapter sends a picture or video its messenger shows inline as one, and anything else as a file. Uploads share the adapter's one write line with `POST /send`: one at a time, at most four admitted, and the next is `429 RATE_LIMITED` having changed nothing. A file larger than the feature's `maxBytes` is `400 INVALID_REQUEST`, refused before it is read whole when the length says so. A caption is `400 INVALID_REQUEST` where the feature declares `caption: false` or past its `captionMaxLength` code points. `replyTo` is as for `POST /send`, `501 NOT_SUPPORTED` without `messages.reply`. Every error but `INTERNAL` means nothing was sent; an upload whose outcome is uncertain is never retried by the adapter.

post.summary: Replace the text of a message this account sent.
post.description: Feature `messages.edit`. Text that is empty or longer than the feature's `maxLength` code points is `400 INVALID_REQUEST`, and so is text the message already has; a message older than `maxAgeSeconds`, or one the messenger does not let this account edit, is `403 FORBIDDEN`. The answer carries the message as the messenger now stores it. Edits share the write line with `/send`, and an edit whose outcome is uncertain is never retried.

Feature `messages.delete`. With the feature's `forEveryone: true` the message is removed for every participant, otherwise only for this account. A message the messenger does not let this account delete is `403 FORBIDDEN`; one this account cannot see is `404 NOT_FOUND`. Deletes share the write line with `/send`, and a delete whose outcome is uncertain is never retried.

post.summary: Set this account's reactions on a message.
post.description: Feature `reactions.send`. `emojis` becomes this account's reactions on the message, replacing what it had; `[]` removes them. More than `maxPerMessage`, or the same emoji twice, is `400 INVALID_REQUEST`; an emoji the room does not allow is `403 FORBIDDEN`. The answer carries the message's reactions afterwards. Reactions share the write line with `/send`.

post.summary: Mark a room read up to a message.
post.description: Feature `read.mark`. Marks the room read up to and including `messageId`, as the messenger's own client does when a person reads it; the messenger may tell the other participants. Marking what is already read changes nothing and succeeds. Read marks share the write line with `/send`.

InvalidRequest.description: `INVALID_REQUEST`: malformed, or outside a declared limit; nothing changed.

Forbidden.description: `FORBIDDEN`: the messenger does not let this account do this here; nothing changed.

NotFound.description: `NOT_FOUND`: no such room, message or attachment for this account.

RateLimited.description: `RATE_LIMITED`: the adapter's line is full or the messenger asked it to slow down; nothing changed.

Internal.description: `INTERNAL`: the adapter failed; the message says nothing about the account. On a write, the outcome is unknown.

NotSupported.description: `NOT_SUPPORTED`: this adapter does not declare the route's feature.

ReauthRequired.description: `REAUTH_REQUIRED`: the messenger no longer accepts the adapter's session; nothing changed.

ErrorCode.description:
Known codes, each with its one HTTP status. The set grows: keep a default branch.

- `UNAUTHORIZED` 401: the bearer token is missing or wrong.
- `INVALID_REQUEST` 400: the request is malformed or outside a declared limit.
- `NOT_FOUND` 404: no such route, room, message or attachment for this account.
- `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` 405: the route answers another method, named in `Allow`.
- `NOT_SUPPORTED` 501: the adapter does not declare the route's feature.
- `RATE_LIMITED` 429: the adapter's line is full or the messenger asked it to slow down.
- `BUSY` 503: the adapter holds as many streams as it will.
- `INTERNAL` 500: the adapter failed; the message says nothing about the account. On a write, the outcome is unknown.
- `FORBIDDEN` 403: the messenger does not let this account do this here (a channel it cannot post in, a group that restricted or banned it).
- `REAUTH_REQUIRED` 503: the messenger no longer accepts the adapter's session (signed out, revoked or expired); a person signs in again where the adapter runs.

version.description: The `info.version` of this document the adapter answers. A client checks it against its own caret range before anything else.
The adapter's own release, independent of the contract version.

id.description: Stable, e.g. `telegram`. Do not infer features from it; read `features`.

icon.description: Present when `GET /icon` answers the provider's icon: an opaque version of its bytes, changing whenever they do. Absent when the adapter has none; a client then draws its own mark.

kind.description: `user`: the adapter acts as the person, seeing what their own client sees. `bot`: a bot account, seeing only where it was added. `official`: an official or business account. A client says which it is showing.

revision.description: Opaque content hash of the declaration.

Features.description: Supported features by id, each with the limits its messenger enforces. Absent means unsupported. Ids under `x-<provider>.` are provider extensions; ignore any id you do not know.

FeatureRoomsList.description: List the conversations the account can see: `GET /rooms`.

FeatureMessagesRead.description: Read a room's messages, oldest first: `GET /messages`.

paging.description: `none`: only the newest window. `before-id`: earlier pages before a message id.

resume.description: `none`: a reconnection starts from now. `cursor`: a reconnection resumes from per-room cursors without a gap.

events.description: The events this adapter sends besides `ready`, `message`, `cursor`, `ping` and `error`: any of `message.edited`, `message.deleted` and `reactions.updated`, or a provider's own `x-<provider>.` events. Absent means none of them. Resume replays `message` only: an edit, a deletion or a reaction missed while disconnected is not sent again, so a client that must be exact rereads `/messages`.

maxLength.description: Longest text the messenger accepts, in Unicode code points.

receipt.description: `accepted`: the messenger took the request, nothing more is known. `stored`: the answer carries the id of the message the messenger stored.

FeatureMessagesReply.description: Send a message as a reply to another in the same room: `replyTo` on `POST /send`. Declared only beside `messages.send`.

FeatureMessagesEdit.description: Replace the text of a message this account sent: `POST /edit`.

maxLength.description: Longest text the messenger accepts in an edit, in Unicode code points.

maxAgeSeconds.description: How long after sending a message can still be edited. Absent when the messenger sets no age limit.

FeatureMessagesDelete.description: Delete a message: `POST /delete`. The messenger decides whose messages this account may delete; where it does not let it, the answer is `403 FORBIDDEN`.

forEveryone.description: Whether deletion removes it for every participant rather than only this account.

FeatureReactionsRead.description: Messages carry their reactions: `Message.reactions`, and `reactions.updated` on the stream when `messages.stream` lists it in `events`.

FeatureReactionsSend.description: Set this account's reactions on a message: `POST /react`. Declared only beside `reactions.read`.

maxPerMessage.description: Most reactions this account may leave on one message. Absent when the messenger sets no limit.

FeatureReadMark.description: Mark a room read up to a message, as the messenger's own client does when a person reads it: `POST /read`.

FeatureTypingSend.description: Reserved. Show that the account is typing: `POST /typing`.

FeatureThreadsRead.description: Reserved. Read a thread under a message: `GET /thread`. A thread is not a room; a room is the conversation.

FeatureAttachmentsRead.description: Messages carry `attachments`, and `GET /media` answers their bytes.

FeatureAvatarsRead.description: Messages carry their sender's profile picture: `Message.senderAvatar`, an id `GET /media` answers. Declared only beside `attachments.read`, whose route serves the bytes.

maxBytes.description: Largest file the adapter takes from this account, in bytes: the smaller of the messenger's limit and the adapter's own.

caption.description: Whether a file can carry text with it.

captionMaxLength.description: With `caption: true`, and only then: the longest caption the messenger accepts, in Unicode code points.

receipt.description: As for `messages.send`: `stored` means the answer carries the message the messenger stored.

RoomFeatures.description: A room's own features where they differ from the declaration. A key replaces the declared value of that feature for this room, and `false` means the feature is unsupported here; an absent key leaves the declaration as it is. Only declared features appear: a room narrows the declaration and never adds to it.

Room.description: A conversation. A key that does not apply is absent, never null or false.

id.description: Opaque. Compare, store and send it back as the string it is; never as a number.

title.description: What the messenger's own client shows as the room's name.

kind.description: `direct`: one other account (person or bot). `group`: several members who can all write. `channel`: a broadcast most members only read.

unread.description: The messenger's own unread count for this account.

lastMessage.description: The newest message, for a list preview.

text.description: At most its first 200 code points. Empty when the message has no text (a photo, a sticker).

complete.description: `false` when the adapter stopped at its own cap and more rooms exist.

Attachment.description: A file a message carries. A key that does not apply, or that the messenger does not say, is absent.

kind.description: `file`: something to download. `image`: a still picture. `video`. `audio`: music or a recording. `voice`: a voice note. `sticker`. `animation`: a looping silent clip, such as a GIF.

name.description: The file name it was sent with. Somebody else chose it: show it, never use it as a path.

mimeType.description: As the messenger reports it. `GET /media` serves a type by its own rule, not by this.

Reaction.description: One reaction on a message: an emoji, how many accounts chose it, and whether this account is one of them. Only reactions the adapter can name as a Unicode emoji appear; a messenger's custom or paid reactions may be left out.

emoji.description: The emoji as Unicode text, exactly as `POST /react` takes it back.

Message.description: A key that does not apply is absent.

id.description: Opaque; send it back as is.

sender.description: The name the messenger shows for the sender (a channel's own title for its posts).

senderAvatar.description: The sender's profile picture as the messenger shows it: an opaque id for `GET /media`, like an attachment's. A new picture carries a new id. Present only when the adapter declares `avatars.read` and the sender has a picture it can serve; absent, a client draws its own placeholder.

text.description: Empty when the message carries no text.

kind.description: `media`: a photo, file, sticker, voice and so on, with `text` its caption; its files are in `attachments` when the adapter declares `attachments.read`. A link preview is not media. `service`: a join, a title change and the like.

replyTo.description: The id of the message this replies to.

groupId.description: Shared by messages the messenger shows as one album (such as a Telegram media group): they come from one sender and are consecutive in the room, so a client may draw them as one. Each stays its own message for replies, reactions, edits and deletion. Absent when the message stands alone.

attachments.description: The files the message carries, in the order the messenger shows them. Present only when the adapter declares `attachments.read` and the message carries a file it can describe.

reactions.description: The reactions on the message, in the order the messenger shows them. Present only when the adapter declares `reactions.read` and the message has reactions it can name.

Cursor.description: Room id to the id of the last message the stream sent for it.

reactions.description: The message's reactions as they now are; empty when it has none the adapter can name.

replyTo.description: With `messages.reply`: the id of the message in the same room this one answers. An adapter that does not declare `messages.reply` answers it with `501 NOT_SUPPORTED` and sends nothing.

file.description: Exactly one file. Its part's file name and content type are the file's.

caption.description: With `caption: true`: text sent with the file, at most `captionMaxLength` code points.

text.description: The whole new text, at most the feature's `maxLength` code points.

message.description: The message as the messenger now stores it.

emojis.description: This account's reactions on the message after the write, replacing whatever it had; `[]` removes them. At most the feature's `maxPerMessage`.

reactions.description: The message's reactions after the write; empty when it has none the adapter can name.

messageId.description: The newest message read: it and every message before it in the room are marked read.
